transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi, doctor. Thank you so much for seeing me. Um, I hope I'm not wasting your time or anything, but I'm here because... well, I guess I've been making some slight adjustments to my routine lately. Just regarding elevators. 

It's probably not a huge deal, but I've started sort of planning my days around not using them. Like, at home, I just take the five flights of stairs now. Which, you know, is actually really good for my health, right? Extra cardio? But... I guess it's getting a little inconvenient for my work. I actually turned down a training workshop recently because it was in a high-rise. And, um... I even stopped doing home visits with one of my older computer students because his building doesn't really have a good alternative to the elevator. 

I feel awful about letting him down, to be honest. I just really, really prefer to avoid them if I can. Is... is that the sort of thing you handle here? Am I explaining that right?
When you think about elevators, do you feel anxious or afraid while you're in them, or is it more about preferring to avoid them for other reasons?

Um, well... I guess it is a bit of fear, if I'm being completely honest. I mean, logically, I know an elevator in a normal office block is probably perfectly safe, right? But... when I look at those older doors, like the ones in my apartment building, or the ones at my work, my mind just sort of... it treats it like I'm about to get trapped in there. Or like the car is just going to drop. 

Which I know is silly! Part of me totally knows that sounds way over the top, and I'm probably just making a mountain out of a molehill. But I do get this nervous feeling when I look at them, so I just avoid it to save myself the trouble. Does that make sense? I hope I don't sound too ridiculous saying that out loud.

When you think about elevators or feel nervous about using one, do you find yourself having repeated, unwanted thoughts that you can't seem to get rid of, or do you feel like you have to do something specific or ritualistic to manage that anxiety?

Um, no, no, not at all. I don't really have any, like, rituals or anything like that. I'm definitely not doing anything weird like tapping the walls or counting or... whatever it is people do. I hope you didn't think I was doing anything strange like that? 

And as for unwanted thoughts, I mean... no, not really. It's just that passing feeling of, "Oh, I'd rather not go in there," and then I just take the stairs instead. Once I'm on the stairs, I'm totally fine, I don't even think about the elevator anymore. I just move on with my day. So, yeah, no obsessive thoughts or anything crazy. I'm pretty normal in that regard, I promise. Is that... is that a good thing? I hope I'm giving you the right kind of answers.
Outside of elevator-related situations, do you find yourself feeling anxious or worried in other parts of your daily life, like work, relationships, or other responsibilities?

Um, no, not really. I mean, I think I'm pretty well-adjusted overall. Work is going really well—I do training and development stuff, and I really like it. And my relationships are fine, too. I don't really worry about that kind of stuff. 

I mean, everyone gets a little stressed sometimes, right? Like if there's a big deadline or something? But it's nothing major, nothing I can't handle. I'm definitely not an anxious person in general. It's really just the elevator thing, and even that, like I said, I just take the stairs and it's fine. 

So, yeah, no other worries or anything like that. I hope that's the kind of answer you're looking for? I just want to make sure I'm giving you a clear picture.
Does avoiding elevators ever cause you a lot of distress or interfere with things that are important to you, like work opportunities or spending time with people you care about?

Um... well... I guess, if I'm being completely honest, it might be causing a little bit of an issue lately. Nothing huge, I promise! Just... minor things. 

Like, at work, there was this workshop assignment I was supposed to do, but it was in a high-rise building, and... well, I kind of turned it down. I made up an excuse, which I know isn't great, but I just couldn't imagine doing all those stairs in my work clothes, you know? And... I also volunteer teaching computer skills to seniors, which I love, but I recently stopped visiting one of my students because her apartment is on a really high floor and taking the stairs just isn't practical. 

So, I guess it is interfering a little bit? But I'm sure I can figure out a way around it. It's not like my whole life is falling apart or anything! I just... I hope it doesn't make me sound like a bad employee or a bad volunteer. I really do care about my work and my students. Does that make sense? I hope I'm not making it sound worse than it is.

When you're not near an elevator and aren't thinking about using one, do you still find yourself feeling anxious or worried about them, or does the anxiety only come up when you're actually faced with the idea of using an elevator?

Um, no, definitely not. When I'm not around them, I don't even think about them. It's not like I'm sitting at home worrying about elevators, you know? 

It really only happens when I'm right there, and I realize I might have to get in one. Or if I know I'm going somewhere that has them, I might think, "Oh, I'll just find the stairs." But it's not a constant worry or anything like that. I'm totally fine otherwise. I hope that's normal? I just don't want you to think I'm obsessing over this all day long, because I'm really not.
When did you first start feeling this way about elevators? Was there a specific event or situation that led to this discomfort, or did it seem to come on gradually without a clear cause?

Um, well... I'd say it's been about seven months. Yeah, around seven months. It wasn't really a gradual thing. I had just moved into this new apartment—it's on the fifth floor—and shortly after I moved in, I had this... I guess you could call it a little elevator scare. 

It wasn't anything crazy, I promise! Just a minor scare. I don't want to make it sound like some big, dramatic event. But I guess ever since then, I've just felt a lot better taking the stairs. 

I hope that doesn't sound too ridiculous? I know it's probably a bit silly for a grown man to let one little scare bother him this much, but I want to make sure I'm giving you the right information. Does it make sense that it would start like that?
